newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy temporarily recalls Iran ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Italy temporarily recalls Iran ambassador.

text.p: Italy will "temporarily" recall its ambassador to Iran after a German court accused Iranian political leaders of ordering the murder of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin, diplomatic sources said on Friday.
The sources said the Italian ambassador would return home early next week ahead of a meeting of European Union foreign ministers on April 29, called to discuss the situation.
Italy is Iran's biggest EU trading partner, importing 17 percent of its oil needs from the country in 1996.
The Italian Trade Commission said total imports from Iran totalled 2.74 trillion lire ($1.6 billion) in 1996 from 2.56 trillion lire in 1995.
"We want to underline...that the European Union has not discussed the possiblity of economic or commercial sanctions towards Iran, much less breaking diplomatic relations," an Italian diplomat said.
The EU action followed a German court finding on Thursday that senior Iranian leaders ordered the killings of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in a Berlin restaurant in 1992.
In Vienna, the Austrian Foreign Ministry said it was recalling its ambassador in Iran in the wake of the German court ruling.

"The Austrian ambassador will be recalled to Austria to give information on the situation," a ministry spokesman told Reuters. "It is a signal of political mistrust against the regime in Iran." ($ = 1697 Italian Lire)
